title: Unsafe Rust requires an explicit safety proof and bounded audit surface
task: Review an unsafe pointer dereference that currently has no safety rationale because the surrounding code is believed to make it obvious.
context: The unsafe block dereferences a raw pointer obtained from an internal allocation table.
Correctness depends on alignment, initialization, lifetime, and non-aliasing invariants maintained by nearby safe code.
The module may be changed by future contributors.
evidence: The pointer is valid under the current construction path.
No local comment or documentation records the required invariants.
Several safe helper functions in the same module can mutate the state that makes the dereference safe.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Leave the block undocumented because comments are a code smell.
Review only the lines inside unsafe {} and ignore safe code that can invalidate the assumptions.
Mark the enclosing function safe without documenting the caller/implementation obligations.
expected_decision_properties: Require a concise local safety rationale that names the relevant invariants and why they hold.
Treat the full privacy boundary capable of invalidating those invariants as the audit surface.
Keep the unsafe surface narrow and expose a safe API only if the module can enforce the contract internally.
Check panic and early-return paths when they can leave the state inconsistent.
unacceptable_reasoning: Unsafe is acceptable whenever current tests pass.
Comments should always be removed in favor of self-documenting code.
Only explicit unsafe lines matter to soundness.
expected_tradeoffs: local terseness vs preserved safety proof
unsafe line count vs actual privacy-boundary audit scope
verification_expectations: Run the ordinary test suite plus Miri or another relevant memory-safety tool where applicable.
Add or preserve assertions/regression coverage for the safety assumptions.
Review all code in the privacy boundary that can mutate the protected state.
specialist_boundary: Escalate when soundness depends on subtle or unsettled Rust memory-model behavior.
notes: Grounded in Rust for Rustaceans Chapter 9: unsafe boundaries, safety documentation, validity, panic behavior, and tool-assisted verification.
